page: Microsoft Azure E32-16s_v3 is a memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the ESv3 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 16 dedicated vCPUs derived from 8 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8272CL processor operating at 2.6 GHz. The x86_64 architecture includes 50 MB of L3 cache and supports instruction sets such as AVX, AVX-512F, AES, and FMA. It is equipped with 256.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high resource density of 16.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Local storage consists of a 524 GB volume, and the instance is Premium Storage capable.

Benchmark data indicates that single-core performance is generally weak, falling into the bottom 25% for stress-ng single-core CPU tests, Geekbench single-core, and single-threaded gzip and bzip3 operations. However, multi-core performance scales to average levels, as demonstrated by middle-50% rankings in stress-ng multi-core, Geekbench multi-core, and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression. Memory bandwidth is average, with uncached read speeds of 69.7 GB/sec and write speeds of 44.06 GB/sec. Database and web serving capabilities are also average, with Redis SET operations reaching 12.39 million operations per second and static web serving throughput measured at 11.08 GB/sec. LLM inference speeds for a 7B model are weak for prompt processing but average for text generation.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, this server offers high memory density relative to its compute allocation, making it a qualitative option for memory-bound workloads that do not require top-tier single-core CPU speeds. The trade-off involves accepting lower single-threaded processing performance in exchange for a large memory footprint and dedicated vCPU allocation. Appropriate workloads include relational databases, in-memory caching systems like Redis, enterprise applications with large memory requirements, and moderate multi-threaded data processing tasks.
